Hello! I'm a rising senior at North Andover High School (NAHS). I am passionate about STEM, with a specific focus on robotics and computational biology. Outside of school, I play volleyball, love listening to music, and enjoy traveling whenever I can.

In summer 2026, I completed six weeks of independent research in Prof. Rouzbeh Amini's lab as part of the Northeastern University 2026 Young Scholars Program. The lab focuses on biomechanics and computational modeling of soft tissue, an intersection that connects directly to my interests in computational biology and engineering.

I was also a finalist for the 2026 ADA Forsyth Student Scholar Summer Program, an NIH-funded biomedical research internship at the ADA Forsyth Institute in Somerville, MA.

Summer YSP Research

Northeastern YSP 2026

For six weeks in the summer of 2026, I worked in Prof. Rouzbeh Amini's Soft Tissue Biomechanics Lab at Northeastern University, where I got to do hands-on wet lab research alongside my project partner, Anjali Misra, under the mentorship of PhD student Guadalupe Garcia.

Our project asked a simple but important question: Does freezing change the mechanical behavior of aortic tissue? Because fresh tissue is not always available, biomechanics labs often store samples in an ultra-cold freezer and test them later. We set out to find whether that storage step changes how the tissue actually behaves.

I learned to dissect porcine aortic tissue, prepare specimens, and run biaxial mechanical tests that stretch the tissue in two directions to mimic how it is loaded in the body, then compared fresh and frozen samples and worked through the data. It was my first real taste of what research is like day to day, and it has made me even more excited to keep going.

Research Interests

My interest in Computational Biology is deeply personal. After losing my grandfather to Multiple System Atrophy (MSA), my father explained that there is currently no cure for this rare neurodegenerative disease. That conversation changed how I viewed science. I realized that when there aren't clear answers, research is how people slowly work toward understanding.

As I explored science beyond my coursework, I became fascinated by how artificial intelligence can be applied to biology. I first learned about AlphaGo and was amazed by how a computer could learn and improve through experience. This led me to read about AlphaFold and how similar ideas could be used to predict protein structures, a problem that had challenged scientists for decades. When I later learned about AlphaGenome, I was struck by how much remains unknown, especially in non-coding regions of DNA.

I'd like to better understand how computational tools can be used alongside biological data to study real diseases like MSA.

Currently Exploring

  • •DeepMind's AlphaGenome and how it predicts the effects of non-coding genetic variants
  • •Research on alpha-synuclein misfolding and the role of the SNCA gene in MSA, Parkinson's, and related diseases
  • •ADA Forsyth Institute research on the oral microbiome and its connection to neuroinflammation

I'm the Lead Mechanical Designer for our NAHS Robotics Team 8568F. Our team was the first freshman team in North Andover High School history to qualify for the VEX State Championship in 2023, with State qualifications each year since. We have also won the Design Award in prior competitions, and most recently took home the Tournament Champion Award at the Pingree School competition in November 2025.

I use Fusion 360 CAD to model and simulate robotic systems before physical implementation, which has taught me the iterative discipline of taking a digital concept and turning it into a working machine.
